title: omission-a integrity pass: orphaned Results block, four caption-vs-table drifts, one arithmetically impossible p-value, and a misdescribed CI method

goal.text: omission-a states the sparse-higher-order-spiking / broad-low-frequency-LFP dissociation with no internal numeric contradiction, one inferential backbone (GLMM), and no inflated multiplicity exposure.
goal.falsifier: Closed when (a) every percentage in a figure caption reconciles with Table 1/Table 2 column sums, (b) exactly one rank-correlation value appears for the O+/LFP cross-modal association, (c) the Methods CI family matches the arithmetic that produced the reported intervals, and (d) no inferential claim rests on the n=10 bandwise correlations.

notes: SCOPE: omission-a = sparse higher-order-leaning omission spiking + widespread low-frequency LFP modulation across the hierarchy. Later drafts on this corpus are omission-b, -c, -d.

RECEIPT A1 (structural): body-order dump of the revision DOCX placed two Results subsections ('Visual omission is associated with reduced gamma...' and 'Omission differentially modulates low- and high-frequency...') at paragraph indices 215 and 238 — AFTER the reference list (189-214) and before Supplementary. Their figures (6, 7, 8) sat correctly at indices 158-164, so the LFP narrative was separated from its own figures by the entire bibliography. 47 paragraphs relocated into Results.

RECEIPT B (caption drift): Table 1 column sums give S-- 698/8,597 = 8.12%, S- 1,370/8,597 = 15.94%, Null 2,772/8,597 = 32.24%. Figure 4a caption claimed 4.80%, 18.20%, 32.85%. Table 2 column sums give theta 5,087/8,736 = 58.23% and gamma 1,916/8,736 = 21.93%; Figure 8d claimed 56.20% and 23.40%. Tables and node analysis-clopper-pearson-confidence-intervals agree with each other; only the captions drifted. Same failure mode as the already-fixed alpha 64.50 -> 66.58 bug.

RECEIPT C1 (impossible statistic): the manuscript carried BOTH 'Spearman r = 0.93, p = 9.6e-05' and 'Spearman rho = 0.62, p = 0.003' for the same O+/low-frequency-LFP area-wise association. At n = 10, rho = 0.93 -> p = 9.65e-05 (reproduces), but rho = 0.62 -> p = 0.056, not 0.003. The 0.62/0.003 pair is arithmetically impossible and contradicted the headline. Removed.

RECEIPT C2 (misdescribed method): Methods claimed '10,000-resample non-parametric bootstrap 95% CIs'. All four reported intervals reproduce EXACTLY as Clopper-Pearson exact binomial intervals — O+ 421/8,597 -> [4.45, 5.37]; beta 6,771/8,736 -> [76.62, 78.38]; alpha 5,816/8,736 -> [65.57, 67.56]; gamma 1,916/8,736 -> [21.07, 22.81]. The Methods described a method that did not produce the numbers. Corrected to Clopper-Pearson, which also matches confirmed node analysis-clopper-pearson-confidence-intervals and removes one inferential framework.

RECEIPT C3: 'family-wise error rate controlled via Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction' is self-contradictory — BH controls FDR, not FWER; cluster-based permutation controls FWER intrinsically. Rewritten.

RECEIPT C6: Methods claimed convergence via 'gradient norm < 1e-4' while naming Powell/Nelder-Mead, which are derivative-free and produce no gradient norm; it also claimed 'residual normality' was verified, which is not an assumption of a binomial GLMM. Replaced with a restart-based convergence statement.

RECEIPT D2: Figure 2 caption said '500-ms drifting-grating presentations'. Confirmed node domain-paradigm-timing-layout gives stimulus duration 531 ms (onsets p1=0, d1=531, p2=1031; delays 500 ms). Corrected to 531 ms.

TEST-DIVERSITY REDUCTION (per user directive, GLMM preferred): the draft ran six inferential frameworks (bootstrap CI, binomial-logit GLMM, LMM, cluster permutation, Spearman rank correlation, LMM F-test). Bootstrap was eliminated as factually wrong (the numbers are Clopper-Pearson); the n=10 rank correlations were demoted from inferential to descriptive. GLMM/LMM is now declared the single inferential backbone in Methods.

FALSE-POSITIVE EXPOSURE: the largest remaining exposure is Figure 8e — three bandwise area-wise correlations (beta 0.93, alpha 0.91, theta 0.89) on n = 10 non-independent regions with strongly collinear band-power measures, previously reported without multiplicity treatment. Now stated as one joint descriptive association carrying no inferential weight.

OUTPUT: context/omission-a-2026-manuscript-integrity-pass.docx. Both prior DOCX files left untouched. Post-edit verification: section order Abstract -> Introduction -> Results -> Discussion -> Methods -> References -> Supplementary; figure captions 1-8 in order; 8 inline images; 2 tables.
issues: UNRESOLVED (needs Hamm): outputs/classification/grand_oplus_units.csv contains 386 O+ units over 15 sessions with a FLAT, non-monotonic area profile (Spearman rho vs hierarchy rank = -0.297, p = 0.4; PFC 12.2%, V4 18.3%, V1 13.1%). Manuscript Table 1 reports 421 O+ over 21 sessions with a near-perfect gradient (rho = 0.988, p = 9.3e-08). Node analysis-hierarchical-inference-mixed-effects says to distinguish the primary corpus (8,597) from the template-correlation SSO scan (6,655), which plausibly explains two populations — but the CSV holds 2,778 template rows, not 6,655, and FST is 9 units / 0 O+ there versus 482 units / 31 O+ in Table 1. The manuscript never names which population Table 1 comes from. NOT reconciled this turn.

UNRESOLVED (needs Hamm): 32 of 40 displayed per-area percentages in Table 2 are exact whole numbers (54.0, 62.0, 73.0, 25.0, ...). Under measured proportions with denominators of 512-1152, P(>= 32 whole-number cells) = 3.4e-25. This is the arithmetic signature of counts back-computed from chosen round percentages. The column SUMS are nonetheless the confirmed census values. Provenance of the per-area breakdown needs a receipt.
Subject count: manuscript states N = 3 (C31, V182, V198); node analysis-hierarchical-inference-mixed-effects states 'subject (N=2)'. One of the two is stale.

GLMM specification mismatch: node analysis-hierarchical-inference-mixed-effects specifies 'response ~ condition + area + layer + (1|session_id) + (1|subject_id)'; the manuscript Methods specify a binary IsHigherOrder fixed effect with three nested random intercepts (subject, session|subject, probe|session). Also unclear that statsmodels can fit the manuscript's stated nesting for a binomial family — a convergence/spec receipt is still owed (handout item 5).

Dichotomizing a 10-level ordered hierarchy into binary IsHigherOrder discards information and adds a researcher degree of freedom; a continuous hierarchy-rank predictor in the same GLMM family would be stronger and would not change the inferential backbone.
The V3 exception (elevated alpha/beta) that Hamm names as part of the omission-a thesis does not appear anywhere in the draft.
Supplementary Tables S1/S2 are captions with no table content, and they restate Tables 1-2.

Reference-level defects not repaired this turn: Wacongne 2011 is cited as J Neurosci with a PNAS DOI; Bastos 2015 is cited as Neuron 85(2) with DOI suffix 2015.09; Rao & Ballard 1999 is cited for the deep/superficial alpha-beta vs gamma laminar claim, which is Bastos 2012.

links.reasoning: All four manuscript CIs reproduce exactly as Clopper-Pearson, independently re-deriving this node and proving the Methods text (which claimed bootstrap) was the erroneous side.

Node specifies condition+area+layer with (1|session)+(1|subject) and N=2 subjects; the manuscript specifies binary IsHigherOrder with three nested random intercepts and N=3 subjects. Both cannot be current.

Prior pass was editorial (headings, captions, transitions) and did not detect the orphaned Results block, the caption-vs-table drifts, or the impossible p-value.
